source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
DartPoints Asheville publishes 1.5 MW of IT capacity. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that is roughly 38 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation density, it is roughly 150 racks. The operator has not published redundancy tier, cooling architecture, or power usage effectiveness, so no further infrastructure claims can be made from the available data.

Among the five North Carolina facilities on this site that publish a megawatt figure, DartPoints Asheville ranks fifth, meaning it is the smallest by published IT load in that group. Those five account for 51.47 MW combined, and this campus contributes 1.5 MW of that, or about 2.9 percent. Nineteen facilities are mapped in the state in total, and most publish no capacity figure, so the true distribution of North Carolina capacity is larger and less visible than these numbers alone show.

At 1.5 MW, this campus sits well below the scale that hyperscale AI training requires, which typically begins in the tens of megawatts per cluster. It could support inference workloads, edge AI, or smaller model serving, but nothing in the published data confirms any of those uses. Asheville is not a primary data center market, and the campus should be read as regional infrastructure rather than a node in large-scale AI build-out, at least on the basis of what the operator has chosen to publish.
